title: The Ghana betrothal is fulfilled, though not as the court intended: Faraj ibn Ismāʿīl, the amir's elder brother and lately his regent, marries Fatiu, daughter of the old ruler of Ghana, and goes south across the desert to live in her land
source: Trent's account (around the new year of 1355; the exact day isn't given)

title: With Faraj gone south, his seat in the dīwān goes to Yaḥyā Raḥḥū, the Zenata general who led the Volunteers of the Faith against Arghūn and the three crowns
source: Trent's account (early 1355; the exact day isn't given)

title: The Powerful Harem: as the harem grows with the amir's Marīnid and Ḥafṣid brides, it becomes an institution of the crown. The amir is no puppet of it, but cunning concubines flood the court and draw power inward around the throne, to the nobles' chagrin; women may now sit in the dīwān

alternatives.dispersed_harem: education of heirs +5%, court spending efficiency +20%, toward decentralization
alternatives.extravagant_harem: prestige +0.10/month, new artists' skill +10%, court spending efficiency −10%
alternatives.secluded_harem: counterespionage +20%, court spending efficiency +10%, toward traditionalist

source: Trent's screenshot of the Harem Laws screen and his account; date from the save of 16 June 1355

title: Yaḥyā Raḥḥū dies of an illness, aged 54, only lately seated in the dīwān. The court calls it a coincidence
source: Trent's account; date from the save of 16 June 1355

title: Duʿāʾ, the Marīnid wife and the most capable of the amir's wives, takes the empty seat in the dīwān: the first woman of the harem to sit in the council

The local governor at Qurṭuba is seated, after some 250 days of building begun in the summer of 1354: from the old seat of the caliphs the crown's authority now runs up and down the great river through the lands won in 1349
source: Trent's account (seated 15 March 1355, after about 250 days of construction)

title: The estates read off the panel: the crown at 32.4%, the nobility down to 26.2%, the ʿulamāʾ 7.0%, the burghers 10.7%, the commoners 4.1% and the Dhimmī about 19.66%
source: Trent's screenshot of the estate power panel, 19 March 1355 (the Dhimmī share is the remainder; it was off the screen)

title: The remission of the jizya and the new governor at Qurṭuba stop a second Castilian rising in its tracks. The realm is stable, control is growing, and the reconquered lands are being integrated
A daughter, ʿĀʾisha, is born in Granada to Shamʿa, the wife Faraj left behind when he went south to Ghana
source: save of 16 June 1355; that Shamʿa stayed is Trent's account

title: Sovereignty reaches 81, Morocco's influence 4.5; stability 28, income 54 against expenses 45, and the treasury owes nothing
